formula.session-list: Lists the captured market sessions in the period from the session calendar; weekends and holidays are not sessions.
formula.session-count: Counts the captured sessions in the period from the session calendar.
formula.coverage: Expected sessions minus captured sessions; the gaps (excluded, missing, holiday) are named, not filled with zeros.
formula.group-net: Sums signed net lots over the visible rows whose broker maps to this group; the side supplies the sign.
formula.broker-ranking: Sorts the visible rows of one side by signed net lots; at most nine ranks are visible per side per date.
formula.price-reference: Sum of net-buy value IDR ÷ (100 × sum of net-buy lots) over the visible rows — a net-flow implied price reference, not an official close, VWAP, cost basis or executable quote.
formula.price-change: The later reference minus the earlier reference of the same kind.
formula.streak: Checks the five most recent actual market sessions; holidays do not break a streak, while a missing or excluded session means not enough data.
formula.daily-activity: Sums signed net lots per session for one broker code.
formula.session-change: Compares group net lots at the previous captured session with the selected session.
formula.broker-observation: Signed net lots for one broker over the period; no holdings or profit are inferred.
formula.reversal: Both directions observed through one broker code; a matched round trip is not proven.
formula.sensitivity: Group net lots recomputed with one broker moved to the unknown group, compared against the baseline mapping.
formula.event: Company events whose verified publication date is at or before the cutoff.
formula.label-evidence: Raw source labels and profile evidence behind the broker-group mapping; profiles do not establish customer identity.
formula.portfolio-performance: V(t) = sum over owned holdings of quantity × close on each common close date; return = V(end) / V(start) − 1. The benchmark is aligned to the same dates.
formula.portfolio-contribution: Contribution = quantity × (close at end − close at start) / V(start), for the holding with the largest absolute share.
formula.portfolio-allocation: Weight = quantity × close at end / V(end); the holding with the largest weight is shown.
formula.portfolio-coverage: Common close dates where every owned holding has a close (and the benchmark when present); the model, currency and data version are named.
formula.portfolio-breakdown: For every owned holding: value = quantity × close; weight = value at end / V(end); contribution = quantity × (close at end − close at start) / V(start), in percentage points.
formula.portfolio-weight-history: Weight on date d = quantity × close on d / V(d), for each owned holding; the weights on one date sum to 1.

portfolio.breakdownDates: Window {start} to {end}. Every value below is the arithmetic of one holding.
portfolio.contributionUnit: Contribution is printed in percentage points: the share of each holding in the portfolio change, which sums to the portfolio return.
portfolio.valueFormula: Value of a holding = quantity × close.
portfolio.weightFormula: Weight = holding value / portfolio total on the same date.
portfolio.contributionFormula: Contribution = quantity × (close at end − close at start) / V(start), in percentage points.

method.title: Method
method.sourceBody: Daily broker summary from Stockbit in NET mode: the visible top nine brokers on each side, net buy and net sell. The side supplies the sign — a broker on the net-buy side is buying, and a broker on the net-sell side is selling. Missing broker entries are unknown, not zero.
method.windowBody: 14 Aug–23 Sep 2026, 26 captured sessions. 13 Aug 2026 is quarantined (overlapping screenshots, 22 rows per side, brokers on both sides). 17 Aug and 25 Aug 2026 are market holidays, and 8 Sep 2026 was not captured.
method.replayBody: Broker data for session D is treated as available at D+1 00:00 WIB. Events use verified publication dates, not effective dates; an event without a verified publication date is unavailable in strict replay. No future points, event text or whole-window claims appear in an earlier view.
method.priceBody: A day's reference is the sum of net-buy value in IDR divided by 100 × the sum of net-buy lots, over that day's visible net-buy rows. Group references apply the same ratio to the group's net-buy rows; XL's selling reference uses its net-sell rows. These are net-flow implied price references — not official closes, VWAP, cost basis or executable quotes.
method.limitsTitle: Visible top nine and rounding limits
method.limitsBody: Only the visible top nine brokers per side per date are known; anything beyond those ranks is invisible, not zero. Net lots and values are integers checked with Number.isSafeInteger; ratios keep their numerator and denominator, and rounding happens only for display.
method.groupsBody: Brokers are labelled app-facing, institution-facing or other / mixed from reviewed public profiles; profiles do not establish customer identity. Every claim carries an evidence strength (Strong, Moderate, Weak, Not enough data) with a one-line reason for that specific statement.
method.codeTitle: What code does, what Qwen does
method.codeBody: App code computes every number, date, group net and the list of approved claims directly from the rows. Qwen only picks approved claim IDs, orders them and chooses an allowed wording variant; it cannot introduce numbers, sources or new claims, and an answer that references anything outside the approved list is rejected before it renders.
method.costBody: A US$270/month engine covering 1,000 stocks works out to about US$0.11 per active client. Illustrative scenario, data fees and production operations excluded.
method.risksBody:
Only a visible top-nine sample: gaps are named as unknown, never filled with zeros.
Broker group labels are judgement: every label carries evidence strength and a one-line reason, and profiles never establish customer identity.
Replay timing could leak future data: strict cutoff checks reject stale or out-of-context answers before they render.
A model could invent numbers: Qwen returns only approved claim IDs and the app supplies all wording and numbers.
method.pilotBody: Whether users understand the Observed / Interpretation / Unknown split; whether evidence drawers get opened; whether the morning brief changes how they read a stock's story; and whether any answer ever cites a fact outside the visible window.
method.validatorBody: This runs the real response validator against the approved claims for the {date} snapshot. First a plan the validator must reject: a claim that is unavailable at the cutoff, or an ID that does not exist. Then a clean plan.
method.toolsIntro: Replay Radar operates on the verified SINI replay at the latest captured session. The pinned Claim Check example below stays on its own fixed snapshot. Every number opens its evidence.

step1.title: Morning brief, 25 Aug
step1.body: The 25 Aug morning runs on the 24 Aug snapshot, available 25 Aug 00:00 WIB, compared with 21 Aug. The banner shows the market is closed today (holiday).

step2.title: SINI replay on 24 Aug
step2.body: Story, Health and Flow show only sessions up to 24 Aug. No September fact exists anywhere in this view.

step3.title: Simulate a sell
step3.body: The sell sheet checks the five-session streak: it passes, and the sheet flags the weakest link on 20 Aug together with the holiday note for the next day.

step4.title: Advance to 23 Sep
step4.body: Move the scrubber to the last captured session of the window, 23 Sep. Everything published up to that date is now in view.

step5.title: Challenge a thesis
step5.body: The HP question is prefilled. Configure the endpoint and demo token in Evaluator settings on the Guided tour screen to ask live; without them the badge shows the saved Qwen replay or the rule-based preview, whichever applies.

step6.title: Open the HP evidence
step6.body: The evidence drawer for HP in the sellers ranking is open: summary, source rows and method. If you like, also check the CC reversal across 17 to 18 Sep in the thesis buckets.

step7.title: Move TP to Unclassified
step7.body: With TP treated as unclassified, institution-facing totals drop and the Unclassified group absorbs the lots. Claim wording updates, raw rows do not change, and the what-if panel lists what survived.

step8.title: Simulate a buy
step8.body: The buy sheet compares today's net-flow implied price reference with the institution-facing reference for the window. Both are references, never executable prices.

step9.title: Method and the validator
step9.body: Run the validator test: the plan citing a claim that is unavailable at the snapshot cutoff, or an ID that does not exist, is rejected, and the clean plan is accepted. The same validator checks every live Qwen answer.

card.explainOverview: This chart compares broker-group net lots between the selected and previous captured sessions, or cumulatively across the window. Values are observed in the visible sample; group labels are team mapping, not customer identity. Every number opens its evidence.
card.explainBrokerFlow: Observed net flow in the visible sample, never ownership, holdings or intent. A break in a line is unknown, not zero. Group labels follow the active classification; the default {count} lines are this window's largest observed net flows.
card.explainEvents: Company events appear on their verified publication dates, not effective dates, and nothing is announced before its date. Each entry links to its published source. Events explain context only; they never imply a buy, sell or price target.
card.streakDifference: Positive net buying and being the largest net-buying group are different checks. The first asks whether the group bought at all in each session; the second asks whether it bought more than every other visible group.
card.brokerLimit: At most {count} lines at a time, so every line stays readable and labelled.
